subtype: Approach: preparing a plan B in case it rains [Thinking]
passage: Sunday, 9 pm. Party plan for Saturday: the park near our building, cricket, a picnic mat, and a cake in the shade. I felt so proud of it. Then Ammi's phone buzzed with a weather message and I thought: what if it rains? Twelve friends, one wet cake, no place to go. I sat with my pencil for ten minutes. Answer: push the sofa against the wall, roll up the carpet, and play indoor games like passing the parcel and a quiz. Pradeep can bring his speaker. Now the party happens either way. I'm going to write BOTH plans on one page tonight. Rafiq.

qa.q: Where will the party be held if the weather is good?
qa.a: The party will be in the park near Rafiq's building.

qa.q: What did Rafiq worry about after the weather message?
qa.a: Rafiq worried that rain would leave twelve friends and a wet cake with no place to go.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Rafiq use to make the plan stronger, and why?
qa.a: Rafiq could pick a date with a backup day or ask the friends' families which they prefer. A second option protects the celebration so it does not have to be cancelled.

qa.q: How might Pradeep see the indoor plan?
qa.a: Pradeep is given a job, bringing the speaker, so the indoor plan probably feels like a real part of the party and not a second-best.

grounding: A boy plans a park party, asks what if it rains, and prepares an indoor plan so the celebration is not cancelled.

subtype: Approach: preparing a plan B in case it rains [Thinking]
passage: Abhinav wanted his party at the mango orchard behind the village school, with races between the trees. He had drawn a map. Then his friend Afreen from next door, reading it, looked up at the sky. "It's the monsoon," she said. Abhinav frowned and thought out loud. "If it rains, the orchard turns to mud. Nobody will race. Then everyone goes home, and no party." He chewed his pencil. "Our front room. If we push the charpai and the trunk to the wall, there's space for musical chairs and dumb charades." He wrote 'PLAN B: front room' at the bottom of the map. On Saturday at four, the sky opened. By quarter past, twelve kids were shrieking round the chairs in the front room.

qa.q: Where did Abhinav want to hold his party?
qa.a: At the mango orchard behind the village school.

qa.q: What was Abhinav thinking when he chewed his pencil?
qa.a: He was worried rain would turn the orchard to mud and end the party, and was working out where else they could play.

qa.q: What else could Abhinav add to plan B?
qa.a: A few indoor games ready and a helper to move the charpai quickly; asking 'what if it rains?' early is what saved the party.

qa.q: How might Afreen see her remark about the monsoon?
qa.a: Afreen only mentioned the sky, but it led to plan B, so Afreen might feel pleased the comment helped save the party.

grounding: Shows a boy planning an outdoor party, asking what happens if it rains, and preparing the front room for indoor games so it isn't cancelled.

subtype: Approach: preparing a plan B in case it rains [Thinking]
passage: Paulo had planned everything for the park near his flat in Porto: football, a water-balloon fight, cake on the picnic table. The night before, lying in bed, a thought poked him. What if it rains? It rains a lot in Porto. If it rained, the park was useless, and his mother might just say, "Let's do it another weekend." He didn't want another weekend. He got up and found his sister Noa. "If it rains, can we clear the living room? Sofa against the wall, rug rolled up. Musical statues and a paper-plane contest." Noa shrugged. "I'll help push the sofa." Saturday dawned grey and wet. Paulo was already rolling up the rug.

qa.q: What had Paulo planned for the park?
qa.a: Football, a water-balloon fight and cake on the picnic table.

qa.q: Why did Paulo get up in the night?
qa.a: He felt worried that rain would get the party put off, and he didn't want to wait another weekend.

qa.q: What else could Paulo prepare for plan B?
qa.a: Paper for the planes and music for the statues game the night before; thinking 'what if it rains?' in advance is what kept the party on.

qa.q: How might Paulo's mother see plan B on the wet Saturday?
qa.a: She won't need to postpone, since the living room is ready, which may leave her relieved and impressed.

grounding: Illustrates a boy imagining rain spoiling his park party and planning to clear the living room for indoor games so it still happens.
